name: National Museum of Tajikistan
funding: No funder, budget or annual report found in the sources opened. Its official site did not load.
watch: Established 1934; renamed National Museum of Tajikistan in 2011 and moved into a new building in March 2013 with 22 halls and over 50,000 objects.
records_note: No museum site loaded; a government portal shows it is a state institution under the president's office, and no reports, accounts or funders appear.

name: Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA)
funding: Founders built its online school at no cost, per 24.kg (2020). Asia Art Archive is a partner on Mobile Library: Kyrgyzstan, April 2025 to June 2026. No funder list found.
watch: Co-founder Bermet Borubaeva also co-founded the TRASH environmental art festival in 2009 and co-curates it.
records_note: No BiSCA website was found; searches show only Asia Art Archive as a project partner, with no reports, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Centro de Arte La Estancia
funding: PDVSA, Venezuela's state oil company, runs the centre as its cultural arm. It still held shows in Caracas in June 2025. PDVSA remains under US blocking sanctions.
watch: General licence 52 (March 2026) permits some PDVSA dealings but leaves it listed. Its Maracaibo branch also runs shows.
why_flagged: PDVSA, Venezuela's state oil company, runs the centre as its cultural arm. It still held shows in Caracas in June 2025. PDVSA remains under US blocking sanctions.
records_note: Its parent PDVSA's website did not load and a search found only a 2010 PDVSA annual report, so its records are unchecked.

name: Lugar de la Memoria, la Tolerancia y la Inclusión Social (LUM)
funding: Peru's Ministry of Culture pays the budget (S/ 1.84M in 2023). Small grants came from the Gerda Henkel and Ford foundations and the German, Spanish and French embassies.
watch: The Culture Ministry removed director Manuel Burga in January 2025 without explanation and barred a Palestinian film in October 2026. Miraflores shut it in 2023.
why_flagged: Peru's Ministry of Culture pays the budget (S/ 1.84M in 2023). Small grants came from the Gerda Henkel and Ford foundations and the German, Spanish and French embassies.
records_note: It posts annual memorias for 2022 and 2023, names its funders and its Patronato in the 2023 one, and no accounts are posted.

name: Museu do Amanhã
funding: Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor; Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers; IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.
watch: Shell and Instituto Cultural Vale are named maintainers. Vale's Brumadinho dam collapse killed 270 in 2019. Over 8 million visitors in its first decade.
why_flagged: Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor; Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers; IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.
records_note: Reports for 2020 to 2022 are in its archive, supporters are named undated, the IDG board is listed, and its accounts page failed to load.

name: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
funding: Government of Chile, through the national heritage service of the Ministry of Cultures: CLP 2.15 billion in 2024. A private foundation runs it.
watch: 176,846 visitors in 2024. Deputies voted down its funding in November 2022; the Senate restored it. A 3% cut hit all ministries in 2026.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2011 to 2025, financial statements 2015 to 2025 and its 15-member board; it names no sponsors, only state funding.

name: Museo Antropológico y de Arte Contemporáneo (MAAC)
funding: Ecuador's Culture vice-ministry (merged into Education in 2025) runs and funds it on a budget above USD 2.5M, and pays the city's Malecón 2000 foundation near USD 500,000 a year.
watch: Over 530,000 visits were counted by mid-2022. The state spent USD 451,000 on renovation in 2024 after a dispute with the city over upkeep.
records_note: No MAAC site was found, and the Culture Ministry site that runs it sits behind a bot check, so nothing could be verified.

name: Museo de la Palabra y la Imagen (MUPI)
funding: Private non-profit. AGIAMONDO and the Ford Foundation backed its 2026 archive move; gifts from citizens, the diaspora and firms repay the annexe mortgage. Its site lists no donors or budget.
watch: Founded in 1996 and marking 30 years. Its fund drive 'Un techo para la cultura' pays for the annexe that now holds the archive.
records_note: Names its three-member board on the About page; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published, only a donation appeal and bank details.

name: Kingston Creative
funding: Inter-American Development Bank (US$1.3M over three years), Bank of Jamaica, Digicel Foundation, Barita, Gore, National Bakery, PwC, the Clara Lionel Foundation and the Miami Foundation.
watch: Runs the Kingston Art District and Artwalk Festival; 118 murals painted. First Caribbean NGO to win a UNESCO-Aschberg grant, July 2026.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2021 to 2025, with financial statements in the 2023 report, a donor list and a board page.

name: Barbados Museum and Historical Society
funding: Annual Government of Barbados grant, plus memberships, gate takings, shop sales, ground rentals and consulting fees. The government appoints five of its 14 council members.
watch: Incorporated in 1933 and opened in 1934 in a former British military prison at the Garrison, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
records_note: Posts annual reports 1994 to 2014 with audited financial statements, names its council and lists partners; nothing newer than 2014.

name: Bocas Lit Fest
location: Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago
funding: NGC, the state National Gas Company, was title sponsor through 2024. 2026 main sponsors: Ministry of Culture, JB Fernandes Trust, OCM; Massy and ANSA McAL foundations and Methanex also support.
watch: NGC part-funded 2024 and gave nothing in 2025; its name left the festival title that year. The festival was founded in 2011.
why_flagged: NGC, the state National Gas Company, was title sponsor through 2024. 2026 main sponsors: Ministry of Culture, JB Fernandes Trust, OCM; Massy and ANSA McAL foundations and Methanex also support.
records_note: Annual reports run from 2020 to 2025, the 2020 one with a percentage financial summary; sponsors are logos dated 2026; the board is listed.

name: Museo Soumaya
funding: Owned and paid for by Fundación Carlos Slim; entry is free at both sites.
watch: Name to know: Carlos Slim. Mexico's regulator ruled América Móvil's units dominant in 2014. His CICSA agreed to repair Metro Line 12 after 26 deaths.
why_flagged: Name to know: Carlos Slim. Mexico's regulator ruled América Móvil's units dominant in 2014. His CICSA agreed to repair Metro Line 12 after 26 deaths.
records_note: The museum and its owner publish no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; Fundación Carlos Slim owns and pays for it.
